summary.headline: Grasim Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue hit record ₹50,105 crore (+26% YoY); adjusted consolidated PAT fell 10% after ₹767 crore Nackawic exceptional charge.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 33% YoY to an all-time high of ₹12,747 crore, with standalone EBITDA at ₹4,615 crore boosted by ₹4,000 crore-odd UltraTech dividend. Reported consolidated PAT was hit by an exceptional ₹767 crore charge (₹825 crore standalone) for idling the AV Group NB pulp mill at Nackawic, Canada; excluding it, consolidated PAT was ₹536 crore and standalone PAT ₹3,132 crore. Birla Opus paints grew 35% YoY in Q2 but revenue fell sequentially on flat realisations and seasonal softness, while management guides to 50% full-year growth on October strength. Chemicals and VSF were up YoY, but caustic prices are at five-year lows and epoxy margins are compressed.

financial_highlights.change: 2.6x YoY, led by UltraTech dividend income
Adjusted PAT down 10% YoY; consolidated PBT up 34% YoY

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹1,337 crore, +35% YoY with volume +20%; H1 volume +33%. Sequentially revenue fell on seasonality and flat realisation; institutional sales fell QoQ but grew 59% YoY. Combined Opus and White Putty revenue share in early teens; target is double-digit share for Opus alone in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹2,785 crore, +66% YoY; retail segment already EBITDA-positive. Q2 EBITDA hit by one-time employee costs (~₹10 crore ESOP impact cited); break-even targeted in H2 FY27 and FY27 revenue above ₹12,000 crore.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibres (VSF/CSF)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹5,344 crore, +29% YoY on volume, mix and stable domestic realisation. Management said Q2 VSF margin was about ₹22/kg and guided Q3 as range-bound; sequential profitability fell on sulfur and pulp cost increases.

segments.name: Chemicals (caustic, chlorine derivatives, specialty)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹2,759 crore, +15% YoY. Caustic CFR SE Asia at five-year low of USD390/t; domestic chlorine prices improved. CPVC (50,000 t, Aug 2026) and epichlorohydrin (50,000 t, Oct 2026) commissioned at Vilayat; chlorine integration to reach 67%. Epoxy margins compressed by BPA/ECH price increases and sluggish demand.

segments.name: Other businesses (textiles, insulators, renewables)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue +16% YoY, EBITDA +14% YoY. Renewable capacity 2.2 GWp after adding 269 MW YoY; CCI approval received for Sprng acquisition, closing expected in calendar 2026, which would take capacity to about 10 GW.

guidance_outlook: Birla Opus: full-year FY27 revenue growth of about 50% YoY maintained; H2 expected to be significantly better than H1 with 57-58% of revenue historically in H2.
Birla Opus: target double-digit revenue market share in H2 FY27 for Birla Opus alone; ambition of ₹10,000 crore brand and India's second-largest decorative paints company by exit FY28.
Industry growth expected at 15-20% in H2 FY27 after 16-17% in H1; listed price increases of 14-15%, retained increases of 9-10%.
Birla Pivot: break-even in H2 FY27 and revenue above ₹12,000 crore for FY27.
Standalone FY27 capex of ₹3,157 crore earmarked, of which ₹1,022 crore spent in H1; management maintained the guidance and expects H2 spend to be heavier.
Paints capex overall stays at about ₹10,000 crore (±1%), with the H1 shortfall of ₹300-400 crore mainly franchise and tinting machines.
UltraTech on track for 242.9 MTPA capacity by exit March 2028; Cellulosic Phase I (55,000 t) nearly complete on procurement; Phase II (110,000 t) environmental clearance at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: Standalone FY27 capex earmarked at ₹3,157 crore; ₹1,022 crore spent in H1 FY27; management said H2 will be heavier.
Cellulosic fibres expansion planned at 165,000 tpa in two phases: Phase I 55,000 tpa with procurement nearly complete; Phase II 110,000 tpa with environmental clearance application at advanced stage.
Chemicals: CPVC 50,000 t commissioned Aug 2026 and epichlorohydrin 50,000 t commissioned Oct 2026 at Vilayat; total chlor-alkali capacity about 2.6 Mtpa (1.5 Mt caustic, 1.1 Mt chlorine derivatives).
Vilayat power plant: reliability fixes done, an additional boiler commissioned for redundancy, and grid connection added; management sees no significant H2 volume impact.
Birla Opus network: 1,760+ exclusive franchise stores (about 300 added in Q2), about 150 depots, 61,000+ billed dealers in 12,600+ towns.
demand_pricing: Global CSF prices rose for four consecutive quarters; Q2 FY27 average USD1.85/kg, +23% YoY. China CSF operating rates 93%, inventory six days.
Caustic soda under pressure: CFR SE Asia at five-year low of USD390/t; domestic prices firmed on stable demand and rupee depreciation. Chlorine prices improved, particularly in Gujarat.
Epoxy value chain margin-compressed as BPA/ECH costs rose and demand was sluggish; management is trading volume for margin.

Paints: Q2 net realisation flat QoQ despite dealer price list increases; trade discounts and schemes were higher in Q2 across the industry. Opus October volume growth well above H1 average; secondary sales via contractor scans grew 34% YoY vs primary +20%.
Birla Opus price gap to market leader narrowed to about 2-4% by September, excluding a 10% impact on pricing, from a much wider gap at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.question: Does H2 paints revenue growth need to exceed the 50% achieved in H1 to hit the double-digit share target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 should be significantly better than H1 and reiterated 50% YoY growth guidance for the full year, but did not split H2 growth further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there slippage in paints capex versus the ₹10,000 crore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the overall paints capex remains about ₹10,000 crore (±1%), with ₹300-400 crore less spent so far, mainly on franchise and tinting machines.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for VSF profitability in Q3 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 prices were held stable and Q3 is expected to be range-bound, with sulfur easing from October; sulfur inventory is under two weeks and should be restocked from December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Nackawic pulp mill get a ₹625 crore funding infusion, and what is the benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Grasim holds 45% of the entity and will contribute its share of closure and liability costs; the mill was loss-making with reliability and cost issues, and idling from October 2026 lowers operating and fixed costs. Grasim sourced about 20% of its pulp from the mill and has covered supply from other sources; payback is expected within four years.

qa_highlights.question: Did Birla Opus gain revenue market share in Q2, and were discounts higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Opus did not gain revenue share in Q2 as larger competitors' primary sales were higher than expected. Industry trade discounts were higher in Q2 from wholesale schemes, while Opus discounts were lower; the gap to the leader was cut to 2-4%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 paints growth, and what is the industry growth view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects industry growth of 15-20% in H2 and Opus growth of about 50%, citing reach expansion, contractor advocacy and regional festival campaigns. Industry H1 growth was 16-17%, with 8-9% from price and 7-8% from volume.

risks_watch: Birla Opus H2 target: management guides to about 50% FY27 paints growth and double-digit market share in H2 FY27, but Q2 gained no revenue share and H1 growth was driven by primary sales; October volume strength is the only evidence so far.

Paints profitability: management said crude-linked raw material costs moved from pre-war 65-70% to 90-110% and suppliers have not cut prices; Opus is buying at higher costs while cutting its price gap to the leader to 2-4%.
VSF margins: Q2 margin about ₹22/kg; management guided Q3 range-bound but gave no Q4 guidance; sulfur inventory under two weeks, restocking from December, pulp prices not moderating.

Chemicals: caustic CFR SE Asia at USD390/t, a five-year low; epoxy margins compressed by BPA/ECH costs with volume traded for margin; management said Q4 may be a bit better but cautioned heavily on forecasts.

Nackawic/AV Group NB: ₹825 crore standalone and ₹767 crore consolidated exceptional charge; a ₹625 crore funding contribution at 45% stake with a stated four-year payback; further closure liabilities are not quantified.
Birla Pivot: break-even targeted in H2 FY27 and FY27 revenue above ₹12,000 crore; one-time employee costs (~₹10 crore ESOP) hit Q2 EBITDA, and the B2B segment's profitability path is still unproven.
Sprng acquisition: CCI approval received and closing targeted in calendar 2026; the 10 GW pro forma capacity depends on closure, and the 20 GW ambition is unquantified.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the paints H2 ramp and on the H2 festive start, citing October volumes and the 50% FY27 growth guidance without a split. Noticeably cautious and evasive on Q2 market share, discounting, and chemicals outlook. They declined to give quantified Q3/Q4 VSF or epoxy guidance and repeatedly stressed that the reported revenue market share is only a derived estimate.

adds.what: Cellulosic fibres Phase II 110,000 t/yr (environmental clearance at advanced stage)

growth.why: Management reiterates Birla Opus FY27 revenue growth of about 50% (H1 ~₹3,000 cr, +50%) and Birla Pivot FY27 revenue above ₹12,000 cr, backed by Opus network expansion, CPVC and ECH commissioning and a 165,000 t cellulosic expansion, but no quantified order book underpins the paints H2 ramp, so backing is only partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Caustic CFR SE Asia at USD390/t (five-year low), epoxy margins compressed, VSF Q2 margin about ₹22/kg with Q3 guided range-bound, and paints raw material costs at 90-110% of crude-linked basis vs 65-70% pre-war with no supplier price cuts.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CPVC 50,000 t (Aug 2026) and epichlorohydrin 50,000 t (Oct 2026) already commissioned at Vilayat, lifting chlorine integration to 67%; Cellulosic Phase I 55,000 t is nearly complete on procurement, targeted about Q2 FY28, and Opus added about 300 franchise stores in Q2 to 1,760+.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Birla Opus H1 volume +33% and October volume well above H1 average, with management guiding H2 significantly better than H1 and industry growth of 15-20% in H2 after 16-17% in H1, though Q2 gained no revenue share.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone FY27 capex of ₹3,157 crore is earmarked with ₹1,022 crore spent in H1 and H2 expected heavier; Cellulosic Phase II of 110,000 t is at advanced environmental clearance stage, so a formal capex approval is probable, though the Sprng acquisition closing (10 GW pro forma) is still pending.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management maintained (did not raise) Opus 50% FY27 growth, Pivot above ₹12,000 crore and H2 break-even, and gave no quantified Q3/Q4 VSF or epoxy guidance, while Q2 gained no revenue market share.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opus 50% growth and double-digit H2 share rely on an H2 ramp with only October volumes as evidence, Pivot break-even in H2 is unproven with a ₹10 crore one-time ESOP hit, and chemicals and VSF margins are under pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Opus is pushing reach via 1,760+ exclusive franchise stores, about 150 depots and 61,000+ billed dealers, and regional festival campaigns, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Sprng acquisition closing (10 GW pro forma)
rows.why: CCI approval received and closing targeted in calendar 2026, which would take renewable capacity from 2.2 GWp to about 10 GW.

rows.label: Nackawic pulp mill idling
rows.why: Idling lowers operating and fixed costs at the loss-making AV Group NB mill after a ₹767 crore consolidated exceptional charge, with ₹625 crore funding at 45% stake and a stated four-year payback.

rows.label: Birla Opus price gap narrowing
rows.why: Price gap to market leader cut to 2-4% by September from a much wider gap at the start of the year, though the 10% pricing impact and higher raw material costs limit the room to hold it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Birla Opus H2 ramp, October volumes and the 50% FY27 growth guidance, but cautious and evasive on Q2 market share, trade discounts, VSF and epoxy margins and chemicals outlook; analysts pressed on the share gains and the H2 growth split.
